bounds: Two observer attempts, one kernel flock, one heartbeat thread per owner, one persisted history bit.
fairness: Stopping an owner assumes fair heartbeat termination and fair processing of the final join/lock release. Hard process death atomically stops all of that process threads and releases its flock.
limitations: All persistent writers run in one process. Graceful shutdown joins the heartbeat before releasing the lock; process death ends every thread before kernel release.
Scheduling fairness, exact metric bytes, disk failures, GPU readiness and Python refinement are not proved.
The lock is scoped to a shared filesystem inode. Replacing or unlinking that inode externally is outside these cooperating-process bounds.
Workload token estimation and the pinned Vast SDK are covered by the owning Python test suite, outside the supervision model.

assumptions: Checked formula in vast_worker_supervision: StopCompletes = (processes.forall(p => threadExit(p).weakFair(s) and finish(p).weakFair(s))).implies( processes.forall(p => (s.phase.get(p) == "closing").leadsTo(Set("exited", "crashed").contains(s.phase.get(p)))))
The property is conditional on its written model fairness and environmental premises. Real scheduler fairness, provider completion and implementation refinement are not proved.
